blocking.section: Runbooks > Ruralz Control rebuild from Git (step 4); Runbooks > Holding deliveries during recovery (step 1)
blocking.issue: The rebuild step 4 command renders with `--env prod` but without `--environments`. The CLI and Configuration model say that without `--environments`, `--env` fetches the Environment from Ruralz Control, and with neither source the render is an error. At step 4, Ruralz Control has not read Git yet, so it holds no Environments. Every candidate `bundle diff` therefore exits 2, no commit ever matches, and by step 4's own rule every Cluster is held and escalated. The rebuild cannot proceed as written. Hold step 1 reuses this command after a restore. There, `--env` would fetch the backup-era `spec.variables`, not the candidate commit's, so a commit that changed variables after the backup renders a different digest and is wrongly rejected. This was introduced in the revised command block.
blocking.evidence: HA rebuild step 4: "Before Ruralz Control reads Git, render candidate commits against each Cluster's Nodes." followed by `ruralz bundle diff ./bundle https://node-a.shop.example:9901 --env prod --admin-token-file /run/secrets/ruralz-admin-token   # exit 0: this commit is served`. CLI and API surface: "`--environments FILE` | Local `Environment` resources; without it, `--env` fetches from Ruralz Control (Planned (M2))". Configuration model: "That Environment's `spec.variables`, read from the file named by `--environments` or fetched from Ruralz Control; never the process environment; with neither source, an error".
blocking.fix: Change the command to render from the candidate commit's own checkout: `git -C repo checkout <candidate>` (or a worktree), then `ruralz bundle diff repo/bundle https://node-a.shop.example:9901 --env prod --environments repo/control/environments.yaml --admin-token-file ...`. Add a sentence to step 4 and hold step 1: "Always pass the candidate commit's `control/environments.yaml` with `--environments`, so each candidate renders with its own variables and never with the Control Store's."

non_blocking.suggestion: A restored `pending` Rollout dispatches as soon as the restored replica elects itself. With no Nodes connected, its plan is empty and it completes before the operator reaches the hold, and its digest may not be the served one (for example, a Rollout that was later rolled back after the backup). Step 3 lists only `canary`, `progressing` and `paused`. Add `pending`, and add Rollouts that became `complete` after the restore with a digest that differs from the served one. Give the remedy: `ruralz rollout start` of the served Revision, which also completes empty, before any Node connects.

After a restore, the recovery ref at the served commit may not descend from the last commit the restored Control Store processed (a backward, non-fast-forward move). The Git watcher's behavior on such a ref is not specified anywhere. Name this as a dependency in OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-3 or OQ-control-plane-and-gitops-1.

Freezing merges does not stop a commit that was merged before the loss from finishing in `promotion.from` during the loss and then auto-promoting into an Environment that has a lost Cluster. Step 5 catches this case only through its "passed a canary elsewhere" exception. Say that committing `requireApproval: true` is the preferred hold, and that a merge freeze is enough only when no promotion is in flight toward that Environment.

The "change the value and Drain Nodes zone by zone" path splits a Cluster across two State Stores for the length of the Drain, which conflicts for a while with Scalability's "Every Node of a Cluster MUST resolve the same State Store". In the corrupted or eviction case, the old deployment is still live, so admission can reach one limit per store. Say to stop or firewall the old deployment first, or prefer the new-Cell row whenever the old deployment is still reachable.

"the published count drops at most 10% (target)" is achievable only under option (a) of OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9. The hold section says the count can collapse after a rebuild until that question is decided. Name OQ-high-availability-and-disaster-recovery-9 as GD-10's dependency, the same way GD-5 names OQ-zero-downtime-upgrades-and-hot-reload-9.
